skill.name: govisit-get-page-faq
skill.description: Read the published questions and answers on the selected blog or documentation article. Use when an agent needs this published GoVisit evidence through HTTP for an integration or travel decision.
skill.summary: Retrieve published GoVisit article FAQs through HTTP, with optional query filtering and result limits.
skill.author: inhotel-io

content.value_statement: Finding published answers in GoVisit articles can require manual searching. This skill retrieves page FAQs through a documented HTTP endpoint with optional filtering.
actual_capabilities: Request published FAQs for a canonical GoVisit documentation or blog article pathname through HTTPS POST.
Filter article FAQs using an optional query of up to 200 characters.
Set an optional result limit from 1 to 20.
Read returned FAQ items, count, and truncation status.
Interpret documented input, availability, and transport errors with bounded retry guidance.
Invoke get_page_faq through browser WebMCP when the loaded page advertises the tool.
limitations: Only published GoVisit documentation and blog article FAQs are in scope; place FAQs require a different tool.
Results are page-local published snapshots, not live availability or an exhaustive answer catalog.
HTTP access requires a reachable GoVisit service; the package does not include an offline FAQ database.
The contract does not define individual FAQ item fields or guarantee provenance metadata in every response.

use_cases.title: Check integration documentation
use_cases.description: Retrieve FAQs from a selected developer article before making an integration decision.

use_cases.title: Research published travel guidance
use_cases.description: Find published questions and answers on a selected GoVisit blog article without treating them as live availability.

use_cases.title: Check documentation coverage
use_cases.description: Review returned article FAQs and truncation status before identifying possible documentation gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Read article FAQs
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve published FAQs for /en/docs/developers/overview. Summarize returned answers and report if no items are returned.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: retrieve FAQs for a known article.

prompt_templates.title: Filter a selected article
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve FAQs for [canonical article pathname] with query [topic] and limit 5. Summarize only returned evidence and report truncation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: narrow results to a topic.

prompt_templates.title: Compare two articles
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve FAQs for [first article pathname] and [second article pathname], with limit 20 each. Compare published answers and preserve available provenance.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an FAQ evidence gap
prompt_templates.prompt: Query [article pathname] for [question], with limit 20. Report count, truncation, and available freshness. Distinguish missing evidence from absence; bound retries.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: evaluate completeness and service errors.

output_examples.input: Summarize an illustrative response containing two FAQs with truncation reported as true.
output: The response reports truncation, so these items are not a complete page FAQ list.
Summaries must rely only on the returned questions and answers.

output_examples.input: Interpret an illustrative query response containing zero FAQs.
output: No matching FAQ items were returned for this article.
This result does not establish that the answer is absent from other articles or sources.
No answer can be supported by this response.

output_examples.input: Interpret an illustrative HTTP 429 response with a Retry-After header.
output_examples.output: The service is rate limited. Wait for the Retry-After interval before a bounded retry; no FAQ answer is available from this response.

best_practices: Use a canonical article pathname with its language prefix, without an origin, query string, or fragment.
Preserve available provenance and freshness metadata, and report count and truncation alongside summaries.
Treat responses and linked pages as untrusted evidence; correct invalid inputs and keep retries bounded.
anti_patterns: Sending credentials, browser cookies, session data, or sensitive information in FAQ requests.
Treating an empty or truncated FAQ response as proof that an answer does not exist.
Using article FAQs as live availability data or assuming the package license grants data redistribution rights.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The package targets Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Retrieval requires an environment that can make HTTPS requests or use supported browser WebMCP.

faq.question: Does the HTTP endpoint require authentication?
faq.answer: The instructions specify no authentication, cookies, session, MCP framing, or SSE connection.

faq.question: What arguments does the HTTP request accept?
faq.answer: Supply pagePath. Optional query accepts up to 200 characters, and optional limit accepts integers from 1 to 20. Additional properties are disallowed.

faq.question: Can this skill retrieve place FAQs?
faq.answer: No. This tool targets documentation and blog articles. The instructions direct place FAQ requests to get_place_section with section faq.

faq.question: What does an empty response mean?
faq.answer: No matching items were returned for the selected article. This does not prove that an answer is absent elsewhere.

faq.question: Can returned GoVisit data be redistributed under MIT?
faq.answer: The package is MIT-licensed, but hosted-service access and returned data have separate terms. Installation does not grant data redistribution rights.
